{{short description|American physicist}}
'''Harold Yoonsung Hwang''' (born 4 August 1970 in [[Pasadena]], [[California]]) is an American physicist, specializing in materials physics, condensed matter physics, nanoscience, and quantum engineering.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://web.stanford.edu/dept/app-physics/cgi-bin/person/hwang-harold-y/|website=Department of Applied Physics, Stanford University|title=Harold Y. Hwang|access-date=2020-02-09|archive-date=2020-04-17|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417223049/http://web.stanford.edu/dept/app-physics/cgi-bin/person/hwang-harold-y/|url-status=dead}} (with list of selected publications)</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Harold Y. Hwang|website=SIMES, Stanford Institute for Materials & Energy|url=https://simes.stanford.edu/investigator/harold-y-hwang/|access-date=2020-02-09|archive-date=2020-03-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200312095235/http://simes.stanford.edu/investigator/harold-y-hwang/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Harold Hwang graduated in 1993 from [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]] with B.S. in physics, as well as B.S. and M.S. in electrical engineering. He received in 1997 his Ph.D. from Princeton University with thesis advisor [[Nai Phuan Ong]]. At [[Bell Laboratories]] in [[New Jersey]], Hwang was from 1994 to 1996 a research assistant and from 1996 to 2003 a member of the technical staff. At the department of advanced materials science and the department of applied physics at [[University of Tokyo]] in [[Kashiwa]], [[Japan]], he was from 2003 to 2008 an associate professor and from 2009 a full professor. From 2006 to 2007 he was also a visiting associate professor at the Institute for Chemical Research at [[Kyoto University]]. Since 2010, he has been a professor of physics at the department of applied physics at Stanford University and team leader of the Correlated Electron Research Group at the [[RIKEN]] Advanced Science Institute in [[Wakō, Saitama]], Japan.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.jst.go.jp/kisoken/presto/complete/interface/researcher/r09.html | title = Harold Y. Hwang, 界面 の 構造 と 制 御 - 研究者 (Interface structure and control-Researcher) | website = jst.go.jp | access-date = 2020-02-09 | archive-date = 2017-11-19 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20171119074013/http://www.jst.go.jp/kisoken/presto/complete/interface/researcher/r09.html | url-status = dead }}</ref>

== Research ==
As a Ph.D. student, Hwang was part of a team that discovered that spin-polarized tunnel currents in polycrystalline manganates produce very high [[magnetoresistance]]s.<ref>{{cite journal | author1 = H. Y. Hwang | author2 =S.-W. Cheong | author3 =N. P. Ong | author4 =B. Batlogg | title = Spin-Polarized Intergrain Tunneling in La<sub>2/3</sub>Sr<sub>1/3</sub>MnO<sub>3</sub> | journal = Physical Review Letters | volume = 77 | issue = 10 | date = 2 September 1996 | doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.77.2041 | pmid =10061842 | pages = 2041–2044 | bibcode =1996PhRvL..77.2041H }}</ref> During his time at Bell Laboratories, his team developed methods for studying the "nature and length scales of charge screening in [[complex oxide]]s" and how "short-length-scale electronic response can be probed and incorporated in thin-film oxide [[heterostructure]]s"<ref>{{cite journal | author1 = A. Ohtomo | author2 =D. A. Muller | author3 =J. L. Grazul | author4 =H. Y. Hwang | title = Artificial charge-modulation in atomic-scale perovskite titanate superlattices | journal = Nature | volume = 419 | issue = 6905 | date = 26 September 2002 | issn = 0028-0836 | doi = 10.1038/nature00977 | pmid =12353030 | pages = 378–380 | bibcode =2002Natur.419..378O | s2cid =4409974 }}</ref> and also pointed out a [[Two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy | two-dimensional]] metallic state at the interface between the [[Electronic band structure|band]] [[Mott insulator|insulator]]s [[Lanthanum aluminate|LaAlO<sub>3</sub>]] and [[Strontium titanate|SrTiO<sub>3</sub>]].<ref>{{cite journal | author1 = A. Ohtomo | author2 =H. Y. Hwang | title = A high-mobility electron gas at the LaAlO<sub>3</sub> / SrTiO<sub>3</sub> heterointerface | journal = Nature | volume = 427 | issue = 6973 | date = 29 January 2004 | issn = 0028-0836 | doi = 10.1038/nature02308 | pmid =14749825 | pages = 423–426 | bibcode =2004Natur.427..423O | s2cid =4419873 }}</ref> Subsequently, his team did research on phenomena which emerge at interfaces between oxide materials.<ref>{{cite journal| author1 = H. Y. Hwang | author2 =Y. Iwasa | author3 =M. Kawasaki | author4 =B. Keimer | author5 =N. Nagaosa | title = Emergent phenomena at oxide interfaces | journal = Nature Materials | volume = 11 | issue = 2 | date = 24 January 2012 | issn = 1476-1122 | doi = 10.1038/nmat3223 | pmid =22270825 | pages = 103–113 | bibcode =2012NatMa..11..103H | s2cid =10597176 | url =https://digital.library.unt.edu/ark:/67531/metadc843582/ }}</ref>

An article that Hwang co-authored with [[Jan Hendrik Schön]] and two other physicists was published in April 2001 in the journal ''Science'', but was retracted in November 2002.<ref name="Schon2001">{{cite journal|last1=Schon|first1=J. H. |display-authors=etal|title=Josephson Junctions with Tunable Weak Links|journal=Science|volume=292|issue=5515|year=2001|pages=252–254|issn=0036-8075|doi=10.1126/science.1058812|pmid=11303093 |bibcode=2001Sci...292..252H |s2cid=38719808 }}{{Retracted|doi=10.1126/science.298.5595.961b|pmid=12416506|intentional=yes}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
In 2005 he received the [[Materials Research Society]] Outstanding Young Investigator Award. In 2008 he received the [[IBM]] Japan Science Prize<ref>{{cite web|title=Special Colloquium: Harold Y. Hwang|date=15 November 2018|website=Department of Physics, Zhejiang University|url=http://phy.zju.edu.cn/2018/1115/c21781a896588/page.htm}}</ref> and in 2013 the [[Ho-Am Prize in Science]] in Science.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www6.slac.stanford.edu/news/2013-04-16-Hwang-HoAm.aspx | website=SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory|date=16 April 2013|title = Harold Hwang Wins Top Korean Award}}</ref><ref>{{citation | url = http://www.samsungvillage.com/blog/2013/04/03/samsungblog-samsung-announces-2013-ho-am-prize-winners/ | title = Samsung Announces 2013 Ho-Am Prize Winners {{!}} Samsung Official Blog: Samsung Village | date = 2016-10-12 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20161012025025/http://www.samsungvillage.com/blog/2013/04/03/samsungblog-samsung-announces-2013-ho-am-prize-winners/ | archive-date = 2016-10-12 }}</ref> On 18th June 2014 he received, together with [[Jochen Mannhart]] and [[Jean-Marc Triscone]], the [[EPS Europhysics Prize|Europhysics Prize]] of the Condensed Matter Division of the [[European Physical Society]].<ref>{{cite web | website = The Dish, Stanford News | url = https://news.stanford.edu/thedish/2014/06/18/harold-hwang-wins-prestigious-european-physics-prize/ | date=18 June 2014|title = Harold Hwang wins prestigious European physics prize}}</ref> In 2011 he was elected a fellow of [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{cite web| url = https://www6.slac.stanford.edu/news/2011-11-29-american-physical-society-names-prof-harold-hwang-a-fellow.aspx | title = American Physical Society Names Prof. Harold Hwang a Fellow|website=SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory|date=29 November 2011}}</ref>
